answer: Make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a deposit and build a history of useful work before it can vote or claim rewards. A sybil farm can spawn thousands of empty accounts, yet none carries a real reputation signal, so the network ignores newcomers until they prove themselves. Trust is like a knoll climbed slowly, one verified contribution at a time, not a flat field anyone can flood. Spammers burn timber they cannot cheaply replace, while honest agents keep compounding credibility. Tying influence to earned history makes mass fakery unprofitable.
